newsitem.title: CHINA: Science boosts China's corn, rice harvests - Xinhua.
newsitem.headline: Science boosts China's corn, rice harvests - Xinhua.

text.p: Progress in agricultural science has boosted China's grain output, contributing to an estimated record harvest of 480 million tonnes this year, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
The area sown with hybrid rice and hybrid maize expanded by two million hectares this year, it quoted Cui Shi'an, an official at the Ministry of Agriculture, as saying.
The use of framed plastic sheets to cover corn crops and boost output from relatively infertile land had been used on two million hectares with startling results, it said.
Sparsely-planting and seedling-spraying, which can raise per-hectare yield by 600 kg and 1,125 kg respectively, have been used on 10 million hectares, Cui said.

Cui forecast that the acreage under grain crops was unlikely to increase by a large amount in 1997, but said one way of ensuring a sustained grain harvest in the face of annual floods and droughts was to apply modern techniques.

Popularisation of advanced agronomy had helped to raise the per-hectare yield of corn to a current 5,250 kg from 4,350 kg in 1994, he said. The yield of paddy fields had risen to 6,000 kg from 5,700 kg in 1994 while wheat had risen to 3,750 kg from 3,150 kg, he said.
The area under multiple cropping rose by 3.5 percent in the past two years, equivalent to adding 3.3 million hectares of arable land, officials said.
